This week's predawn raid by federal agents of the home of a sitting U.S.
lawmaker who is up for reelection just weeks before voters go to the polls
sadly, though perfectly, illustrates what the United States has come to
represent under Donald Trump: An America where the federal government is used
to target the president's perceived enemies. An America where the rule of law
has lost its meaning, an America where fascism no longer hides in the shadows.

In this case, the target was Rep. Ilhan Omar, but we know too well it didn't
start and won't stop with her. Because in Donald Trump's America, racism,
xenophobia, and Islamophobia drive policy. Because in Donald Trump's America,
repression of those who look different or speak out against the president is
the goal.

When they weren't raiding Omar's home, Trump's cronies were continuing their
crackdown on a free press, planning an ICE spying program, and suing
California election officials. Here's more from 'This Week in Democracy - Week
91':

#### **Saturday, Oct. 10 - DOJ Investigating Major TV Networks, Including
Fox**

The _New York Times_
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/10/business/media/trump-justice-
department-tv-networks.html) that Trump's Justice Department launched an
investigation into NBC, ABC, CBS, CNN, and Fox to determine whether they broke
antitrust laws by temporarily suspending pool coverage of the president.

The move comes after a [Sept. 21
tweet](https://x.com/LauraLoomer/status/2102140414367342971) from conspiracy
theorist and Trump adviser Laura Loomer questioning why the Justice Department
hadn't filed an antitrust lawsuit against "the Fake News media outlets,"
accusing them of collusion to refuse to cover the president.

#### **Sunday, Oct. 11 - Trump Airs Taxpayer-Funded Ads Despite Court Order**

After a federal judge
[ordered](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.674638/gov.uscourts.nysd.674638.41.0.pdf)
the Trump administration to stop airing taxpayer-funded campaign-style TV
advertisements, two of the ads [continued to
air](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/12/judge-blocks-trump-
administration-airing-taxpayer-funded-campaign-style-ads/) multiple times in
the hours following the judge's deadline, including into the early hours of
Monday morning. The White House later claimed that the Department of Homeland
Security didn't receive enough notice to cancel the ads in time.

Later, NPR [reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/12/nx-s1-5998976/pro-trump-
ads-taxpayer-funds-federal-judge) that nearly $22 million in taxpayer dollars
had been spent to air Trump's ads, nearly $10 million of which was spent after
Trump's Oct. 5 Truth Social
[post](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117390649505706640) where he
said the government would no longer pay for the ads.

#### **Monday, Oct. 12 - Rep. Ilhan Omar's Home Raided By Federal Agents**

Federal agents [conducted](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-
administration/rep-ilhan-omar-home-searched-federal-agents-criminal-probe-dhs-
rcna602950) a raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's home in Washington, DC, as part of a
years-long criminal investigation involving immigration fraud. The probe,
which the _Wall Street Journal_ later
[reported](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/ilhan-omar-investigation-aims-
to-build-case-for-stripping-her-citizenship-6adf1edc) is part of an effort to
strip Omar of her citizenship and deport her, flies in the face of the Justice
Department's informal "[60-day
rule](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/14/how-pre-election-
search-rep-ilhan-omars-home-breaks-justice-dept-norms/)," which seeks to avoid
any public investigation actions involving a candidate within 60 days of an
election.

On Twitter, Omar called the raid "an attempt to target political enemies and
weaponize federal law enforcement," and added that she "will not be silenced."

Later, the _New York Times_
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/13/us/politics/justice-dept-ilhan-
omar-subpoenas.html) that relatives of Omar have been issued subpoenas as
investigators probe her family's history for any evidence of fraud or false
statements in immigration documents.

#### **Tuesday, Oct. 13 - CFTC Ordered to Retract Referral for Oil Insider
Trading**

Bloomberg [reported](http://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-10-13/cftc-
staff-told-to-retract-analysis-of-suspicious-oil-trades-on-iran) that staffers
at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) analyzing oil trades for
insider trading were told to retract a referral to its Division of Enforcement
by an adviser to the Trump-appointed chair of the CFTC, Michael Selig.

The referral related to trades made about 15 minutes before Trump walked back
a threat to strike Iranian power plants, which ended up being worth billions
of dollars.

#### **Wednesday, Oct. 14 - A $100 Million ICE Spying Program**

The American Prospect [reported](https://prospect.org/2026/10/14/ice-planning-
nightmare-domestic-spy-program-ero-one/) that the Trump administration is
planning to spend $100 million on a domestic surveillance program led by ICE,
that would see more than 140 intelligence contractors with top secret
clearances deployed to dozens of cities across the U.S.

One expert called the program "a nightmare in the making," with others warning
the government will likely use it to spy not only on undocumented immigrants,
but also U.S. citizens.

#### **Thursday, Oct. 15 - Trump Sues California Over 'Likely' Noncitizens,
Without Evidence**

The Trump administration [sued](https://apnews.com/article/california-justice-
department-voting-noncitizens-lawsuit-12c62cf12a7db6480c60975b6dea49b8)
California in an effort to block the state from counting 20,000 mail-in
ballots for the midterm elections until voter eligibility is confirmed. The
Justice Department claimed, without evidence, the ballots were cast by
"likely" noncitizens.

The lawsuit comes after Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan failed to meet
a DOJ deadline to review the list of "likely" noncitizens, which was delivered
on a thumb drive with the password on a sticky note, despite Logan noting he
has no jurisdiction outside the county and that his office can't withhold
ballots or refuse to count them "based solely on unverified allegations."

#### **Friday, Oct. 16 - Katie Zacharia Out as White House Press Secretary**

Trump's new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, was
[ousted](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/16/us/politics/katie-zacharia-fired-
press-secretary.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share) after less than a week in her
position, following a humiliating press briefing on Tuesday and a pair of
[equally](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2111105190883430631)
[embarrassing](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2110904089580044299) interviews on
Fox. Her dismissal came hours after Trump told reporters he encouraged
Zacharia to "reconsider" the position, blaming the media for being hard on her
performance.

Zacharia also stirred controversy for claiming she was an attorney when she
was [nothing of the sort](https://www.wsj.com/business/media/white-house-
press-secretary-katie-zacharia-didnt-pass-bar-exam-714a484e). (Read more of
**Zeteo** 's coverage of Zacharia [here](https://zeteo.com/p/7-things-to-know-
about-the-new-insane).)
